why_preregistered: MANDATORY_IMPLEMENTATION A3: 'Choose the primary aggregation rule before broad game outcomes are unblinded.' A rule chosen after seeing which K wins is not a rule. Everything in this file is fixed now, and the sweep may not change it.

primary_aggregation_rule.definition: For every world and every root edge, sum the SUCCESSOR NODE's visit_count and rewards into a per-action-index accumulator; the aggregate value of an action is sum(rewards)/sum(visits). Final selection is MaxChild on that aggregate.
primary_aggregation_rule.why_this_one: It is not a choice. It is a port of MonteCarloGraphSearch.AggregateDeterminizations plus MCGS.Select(FinalMoveSelection.MaxChild), both present and complete in the official archive. FIDELITY_RULES §1 puts the source archive above every other authority, so where the source specifies the operation there is nothing to preregister except the fact that it is being followed.
primary_aggregation_rule.source_anchor: external_refs/c021_mcgs/extracted/src/MCGS.cs :: AggregateDeterminizations (audit site A1), Select (site not required), Edge.Value (site G3)
primary_aggregation_rule.join_key: action index, exactly as the source matches rootEdge.ActionIndex == edge.ActionIndex. NOT edge list position.
primary_aggregation_rule.which_counter: the SUCCESSOR NODE's visit_count and rewards, because Edge.Value(0) returns Successor.Rewards/Successor.VisitCount and that is what MaxChild selects on. Edge.visit_count is recorded separately but is not the aggregated quantity.

secondary_rules_reported_but_not_selecti.definition: A3's 'visit-count summation': RobustChild over the summed successor visit counts.
secondary_rules_reported_but_not_selecti.status: source-derived (FinalMoveSelection.RobustChild exists in the archive) but NOT the shipped FinalMoveSelection, which is MaxChild (SearchConfig.FinalMoveSelection = 0). Reported for every decision; never used to select.

secondary_rules_reported_but_not_selecti.definition: mean over per-world action values minus z * SE across worlds, z = 1.0.
secondary_rules_reported_but_not_selecti.status: ALGORITHMIC_ADAPTATION. No source counterpart. A3 permits it only as 'an explicitly adapted secondary arm'. Reported for every decision; used to select only in an arm named MCGS_MULTI_DET_ROBUST_LCB, which is never presented as source behaviour.

predicted_win_probability.definition: the aggregate value of the SELECTED action -- sum over worlds of that action's successor rewards divided by sum over worlds of that action's successor visits -- NEGATED when the successor is an opponent node, then clamped to [0,1].
explicitly_not: the maximum over worlds of that action's value
the value in whichever world liked the action most
the maximum over actions of the aggregate value
predicted_win_probability.why: Reporting the most optimistic world as the search's belief would pin the predicted probability near 1.0 at every K, so calibration could not improve with K and the failure would be misread as 'the ensemble does not help'. Asserted by tests/test_c022_aggregation.py::test_predicted_win_probability_is_the_aggregate_not_the_best_world.
predicted_win_probability.scale: rollout returns are in [0,1] (PlayUntilTerminal returns 1.0 for a root-player win, 0.0 otherwise, 0.0 at the turn cap), but Node.Update negates the reward at an OPPONENT node, so an action that ends the turn has a successor whose value is MINUS the root player's win probability. Both the raw signed value and the converted probability are recorded per decision.

AMENDMENT_2026_07_30.what_changed: the sign correction above, and the recording of the raw signed value alongside the probability.
AMENDMENT_2026_07_30.the_error: the original text asserted 'the aggregate value is already a probability'. It is not. Node.Update applies `if (IsOpponent) reward *= -1`, which is correct and load-bearing for SELECTION -- MaxChild still prefers the child best for the root player -- but makes the value of an end-turn action negative.
AMENDMENT_2026_07_30.how_it_was_found: a single calibration row from a SUPERSEDED arm recorded predicted_win_probability = -0.044586. A negative probability is not a marginal reading; every end-turn decision would have scored as a catastrophic Brier miss for a reason with nothing to do with the search, and K would have been blamed.
AMENDMENT_2026_07_30.what_it_was_NOT_found_from: no comparison between K arms, no field score, and no outcome data informed this change. The superseded arm was a K=1 control produced by pre-fix code and quarantined in results/failures/superseded/ before this amendment was written.
AMENDMENT_2026_07_30.why_this_does_not_break_preregistration: DECISION_RULES forbids choosing a rule after seeing which K wins. This corrects a definitional error in the measurement instrument, detectable from a single row's sign without reference to any arm's outcome, and it is applied identically to every arm because every arm is re-run from scratch after it. The alternative -- leaving a known-wrong probability in place to preserve the letter of a timestamp -- would produce a calibration result that is simply false.
AMENDMENT_2026_07_30.arms_affected: none. Every K-sweep arm is run AFTER this amendment. The one arm that predates it is quarantined and cited nowhere.

terminal_scale_rule.situation: Node.Value returns +/-10 for a proven terminal while rollouts return 1/0. If terminals entered the sums, the aggregate would no longer be a probability.
terminal_scale_rule.measured_fact: the frozen C021_MCGS_K1_CONTROL records finalised=0, terminal_leaves=0, lethal_bonus=0 over 226,277 rollouts and 1,281 searched decisions. The tree policy never reached a terminal, so the +/-10 branch never entered a computation at c021 scale.
terminal_scale_rule.rule_fixed_now: per-world terminal_leaves / finalised / lethal_bonus are counted for EVERY arm. If any arm records a nonzero value, the mixed scale is handled by an explicitly documented normalisation and the affected arm is re-run; it is never absorbed silently into a calibration plot. Aggregate.mixed_terminal_scale_detected() raises the flag and tests/test_c022_aggregation.py asserts the flag fires.

graph_reuse_rule.K_sweep_arms: graph_reuse DISABLED in every K-sweep arm, INCLUDING K=1.
graph_reuse_rule.why: Worlds are resampled per decision, so ensemble slot i at decision t+1 is not the world slot i held at decision t. A per-slot statistics table carried across decisions would seed a world's search with statistics conditioned on a DIFFERENT world -- the same contamination as sharing a table between worlds within a decision, one level up. The source avoids this by keeping determinizations alive (CleanUpDeterminizations); PTCG sessions die at search_end, so this port cannot. Disabling reuse in all K arms makes K the only difference between them.
graph_reuse_rule.within_a_decision: each world gets its OWN reuse dict when reuse is enabled at all; a shared dict is forbidden and probe M03c checks no cross-world sharing.
graph_reuse_rule.M04_identity_arm: a SEPARATE arm, MCGS_K1_CONTROL_REUSE, runs K=1 with graph_reuse enabled exactly as the c021 control did, solely to demonstrate reproduction of C021_MCGS_K1_CONTROL. It is not part of the K sweep.

budget_protocols.fixed_total: total simulations per decision constant across K; per world = total / K, with the remainder distributed one per world so the sum is EXACTLY total for every K. Asserted by test_m05_fixed_total_uses_exactly_equal_total_simulations.
budget_protocols.fixed_per_world: simulations per world constant across K; total grows with K. Asserted by test_m06_fixed_per_world_gives_every_world_the_same_count.
budget_protocols.attribution: by SIMULATION COUNT, never wall clock (A4). Elapsed time is recorded separately.
budget_protocols.match_clock: the c021 cumulative 90 s match clock is DISABLED in the K-sweep arms. With K sequential sessions per decision, fixed_per_world at K=8 multiplies search time ~8x; leaving the clock on would make the arm measure clock exhaustion rather than strength. match_clock_exhausted_decisions is reported per arm and is required to be 0 in both sweeps; a nonzero value invalidates that arm's causal comparison.
budget_protocols.world_seeds: from c022_mcgs_worlds.world_seeds(base_seed, decision_index, i) -- a dedicated SHA-256 stream, never the agent generator, so that adding worlds cannot shift the agent's draw order (probe M02c).

calibration_target_M08.what_it_measured: at 12 frozen roots sampled every 9th decision across multiple games, 8 worlds each, 24 source-faithful uniform-random rollouts per root action: mean over root actions 0.200, max over root actions 0.289, rollout from the ROOT before any action 0.201, and the same rollouts scored for the opposing seat 0.601.
calibration_target_M08.terminal_attribution: CONSISTENT. 0.201 + 0.601 = 0.802 <= 1, with the remainder being turn-capped rollouts (0.197). If both seats had been told they win, the terminal owner would have been read off whoever happens to be to act -- the defect c021 found and fixed -- and no world averaging would have helped.

decomposition_fixed_now.shared_by_every_world_and_NOT_reducible_: the rollout's own optimism: 0.201 predicted from the root against an actual field score of 0.111, i.e. about 9 pp.
decomposition_fixed_now.reducible_by_K: within-world action selection: mean over actions 0.200 rises to 0.289 when the best action is chosen, i.e. about 9 pp at depth 1.
decomposition_fixed_now.the_depth_term: c021's runs report 0.79-0.99 predicted over decided rollouts, while this probe measures 0.355 over decided at depth 0-1. The difference is SEARCH DEPTH: UCB drives the tree into lines whose rollouts win, and the selection bias compounds ply by ply. That term is within-world, and cross-world root aggregation attacks it only at the root -- so the ensemble is expected to reduce overconfidence substantially without eliminating it.

calibration_target_M08.M08_pass_condition_fixed_now: K>1 must reduce the gap between predicted win probability and realised outcome, measured as Brier score and log-loss over per-decision (predicted, realised game result) pairs, relative to the K=1 arm on the SAME decisions and seeds. It is NOT required to reach perfect calibration: the measured floor above shows a residual the mechanism cannot remove. A K>1 arm that leaves Brier unchanged within its confidence interval is recorded as no improvement, not as a pass.
calibration_target_M08.why_this_is_stated_before_the_sweep: so that a null result is reported as a null result rather than re-explained against a target chosen afterwards.

REQUIRED_REMEASUREMENT_AFTER_D13.what: the ceiling above was measured with the pre-D13 payload path, which emitted a single option even when a select required minCount > 1. Multi-select decisions now play a DIFFERENT action set.
REQUIRED_REMEASUREMENT_AFTER_D13.frequency_of_affected_decisions: multiselect_decisions was 1 per 12 games in the verification arm -- low, but not zero.
REQUIRED_REMEASUREMENT_AFTER_D13.obligation: tools/c022_probe_rollout_bias.py is re-run after the sweep, and the ceiling it measures is compared against the recorded 0.201 root-only / 0.200 mean-over-actions / 0.088 selection gap. If the ceiling moved, M08's target moves with it and BOTH readings are reported here -- the target is not silently updated to whatever the second measurement says.
REQUIRED_REMEASUREMENT_AFTER_D13.why_this_is_recorded_rather_than_just_do: M08's pass condition is stated against this ceiling. A ceiling that changed after the condition was written, and was quietly replaced, would make the condition unfalsifiable in exactly the way this file exists to prevent.
REQUIRED_REMEASUREMENT_AFTER_D13.status: PENDING -- the sweep holds exclusive CPU (CONTRACT.md §5) and the re-measurement runs after it.
